messages.subject: Limitations to renderPlot
parts:
I am building an application for co-workers. The application has a base set of plots but, because we are an analysis team, I wanted to give them the option to load and use their own custom plots on the application. These plots would later be saved to a server that they would then be able to call on a regular basis for everyone to utilize. 

To do this, I was thinking about having my users input their code as a generalized function with a textInput object. (documentation would explain the prerequisites for adding the function)  The function would obviously be passed as a string from the text input function. I was planning on using eval(parse()) to change this into executable code. But my concern is that I cannot necessarily predict if the returned plot will be rendered. 

I realize that renderPlot can handle base plots and ggplot2 but is there a specific list of the types of plots the renderPlot can or cannot render? Also, as a bonus,  would eval(parse()) be a feasible way to do what I want or is this idea to much? :/ 

Thanks,

Amber

messages.author: 55771919c42cb6a1
messages.subject: Re: Limitations to renderPlot
parts:
renderPlot should be able to handle pretty much any type of plot in R -- at least, any plot that uses the R graphics device.

I very, very strongly recommend against using eval(parse()), because that would allow users to run any arbitrary code on the server. Users could conceivably delete all your files, steal passwords, etc.

-Winston
